title: What If Zombies Took Over the World? (Animated Short Film)
description: What if a zombie outbreak started right now? We trace the chaos from the first emergency alert to total collapse. ... Subscribe for more What If stories and tell me in the comments: what is the first thing you would grab if the alarms started ringing? Chapters: 0:00 Day 1 / 0:52 How Fast It Spreads / 1:37 The Highway / 3:04 Valley Foods / 4:09 The First Night / 5:24 The Power Goes Out / 6:20 The Escape / 7:43 Cities Are Death Traps / 9:17 Greenhill Farm / 10:59 The Herd / 12:52 What Would Really Happen / 13:27 Day 100

art_style: Minimal flat-vector 'black-ball-head stickman' style in a moody, desaturated night palette: deep navy/indigo backgrounds (#141a3a-#2a3470 range) with soft vignettes, glow and light cones; characters are solid black circle heads with white oval eyes/eyebrow strokes and a thin rim-light outline, thin black limbs, one flat colour shirt per character (you = red/coral, Maya = teal with ponytail, Omar = yellow cap + dark, Leo = blue with spiky hair, Daniel = olive-green, Mr. Hale = green with glasses, Ruth = wide tan hat + grey). Zombies = same rig but grey-green skin, glowing white eyes, red wound spots. Environments are simple geometric silhouettes (skyline rectangles with lit windows, shelves made of coloured rectangles, red barn + water tower + chain-link). Second visual mode = line-art infographics: thin white/blue outline icons and pink/red neon stick figures on flat navy with spaced uppercase sans captions (Montserrat/Poppins-like, letter-spaced, small). Third mode = warm sunrise farm palette (lavender-to-peach gradient sky, sun glow). The 9 s cold open is in a richer textured illustrated style (warm street lights, detailed zombie faces) that does not reappear. Thumbnail uses a glossier, rendered-3D-ish version of the hero (goggles, big eyes) not seen in the video.
title_pattern: 'What If [Big Hypothetical] Took Over the World?' + parenthetical genre tag '(Animated Short Film)' - classic What-If question framing, global stakes, no number; the tag signals narrative story rather than a lecture explainer.

thumbnail.composition: Hard vertical split-screen before/after: left half bright sunny kitchen, right half dark blue boarded-up kitchen at night; same character centred in each half at the same scale; white divider line.
thumbnail.text: Two labels at top: 'DAY 1' (white, heavy condensed sans, black outline) over the left; 'DAY 365' (red, same font) over the right. Only 2 words of text.
thumbnail.colours: Left: warm cream/yellow light, red T-shirt, orange juice, colourful cereal. Right: deep navy/cyan shadows, desaturated torn red shirt, brown bat. Warm-vs-cold complementary contrast carries the story.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Character fills ~60% height in both halves; left = huge grin, tongue out, eating Froot-Loops-style cereal; right = wide-eyed, bearded, ragged, gripping a nail bat while rotting zombie hands reach through the wooden boards behind him. Same goggles in both anchor identity.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Time-jump transformation (Day 1 vs Day N) is an instant curiosity gap - viewer wants to know what happened in between; emotional flip (joy -> paranoia) readable at phone size; zombie hands give genre at a glance. Note: thumbnail promises DAY 365 and a goggled hero, but the video ends at Day 100 with a plain stickman - a mild mismatch (possible retention cost), and its art is far more detailed than the video.

hook.first_5s_verbatim: [0:00-0:09 no voice, music only] ... 'What if a zombie outbreak started today? It's 7:42 in the morning. You're half asleep scrolling on your phone when it buzzes.'
hook.device: Silent cold-open flash-forward (9 s): visual tease of the scariest-but-funny image (hero trapped in a car, zombie faces smearing the glass, he smugly sips a soda) with no context, then the title question read verbatim over a title card, then an instant second-person 'you' drop into a precise mundane moment (timestamp 7:42 a.m.) that escalates in ~20 s to an emergency alert and a neighbour chewing something. Stakes and genre clear by 0:50 ('Welcome to day one').
hook.notes: The VO doesn't start until 9.3 s, which is late for YouTube; the cold-open image (car + window faces) pays off at 2:11-2:30, rewarding early viewers. Weakness: no stated promise of what the viewer will learn/see.

beats.summary: Music-only teaser in a richer, warmer illustrated style: a car stuck in a street of zombies, cut inside to the black-ball-head hero as rotting faces press against the window; he goes from scared to smug and sips a soda (a payoff of the 'the glass holds' moment at 2:24). No VO. Fades to black.
VO asks the title question verbatim over a navy city-skyline title card.
'It's 7:42 in the morning' - you in bed scrolling, phone buzzes three times, EMERGENCY ALERT: stay indoors. Second-person present tense.
You laugh it off, a scream, look out the window: neighbour Mr. Collins standing in the road, head tilted too far, chewing. Ends on a zombie face close-up and a 'DAY 1' chapter card.

'How fast it spreads': R number defined, flu ~1.3 vs measles 12-18 bar chart, infection grid filling a city of 1,000,000 in <24 h; then a TV news anchor whose feed cuts to bars + NO SIGNAL (story re-entry).
You pack a bag (kitchen knife 'for tomatoes' joke, 'Bad idea'), everyone has the same thought, 20 MINUTES LATER gridlock; honking draws the dead; hands and a face smear the glass.
You don't scream - the glass holds; wait for them to drift to louder cars, slip out the far door, run past burning bus and abandoned police car to Valley Foods; shutter slams a second behind you.

Five strangers introduced one by one with name + role lower-thirds (Maya nurse, Omar delivery driver with crowbar, Leo 16, Daniel Leo's dad, Mr. Hale 70 store manager with a shotgun 'for raccoons'). 'Now you're a team.'

Supermarket stock count-up (tens of thousands of items), '6 people = months of food', but cities hold only ~3 days of food on shelves; trucks every day... STOPPED. Re-hook: everyone left alive will want what you have.
The first night: barricades, pharmacy-aisle hospital, Hale counting cans (counter ticking), DOZENS of infected pressed against the glass watching the lights.

2 a.m. coughing: Daniel is bitten - 'Don't tell my son.' Explainer aside on real outbreaks failing because people hide symptoms out of fear/love. By morning Daniel walked out alone; Leo finds the note.
Day 5 the power goes out: nobody came to work, grid fails neighbourhood by neighbourhood (dot-grid of lights winking out), freezers stop, silence - then an engine.
Four masked survivors with bats and a rifle: 'They're not infected, they're worse.' Thesis line on text: THE SHUTTER CAN STOP THE DEAD / IT CAN'T STOP THE LIVING.
Omar remembers the delivery truck at the loading dock; blueprint map, icons LOAD -> OPEN THE DOCK -> DRIVE; 'SIMPLE PLANS NEVER STAY SIMPLE.' (explicit foreshadow re-hook).

4 a.m. dock door screams, every head turns, GO!, engine dies twice, the dead run; Mr. Hale walks out alone, fires into the air (BOOM), leads the horde away without looking back; you drive out crying with his shells on the seat.
'Cities are death traps': more people = more infected, nowhere to go, one blocked road = TRAPPED; countryside: fewer people, see danger miles away, grow food, find water.
Day 2 the truck radio crackles: Greenhill Farm, Route 9 - water, fences, room - loops every 10 minutes. Trust debate (could be a trap vs only chance).

'You learn...' list: gas stations are dangerous, noise is your enemy (a gunshot rings a dinner bell for a mile), crowbar > shotgun (quiet, never runs out of ammo, opens doors), sleep in shifts 2 on/2 off, check every car, most infected don't chase unless provoked.

Vine-covered GREENHILL FARM sign, chain-link fence with car hoods welded on, Ruth in a wide hat with a hunting rifle: 'Anybody bit? Show me your arms.' Gate opens; Ruth's backstory (40 years, husband gone, kids in the city); first full night's sleep.

Life on the farm: hand pump, potatoes, chickens ('protein that walks around on its own'), Omar fixes the generator, Maya's clinic, Leo rifle training ('Breathe out... then squeeze'), you become THE SCAVENGER (inventory icons: seeds, antibiotics, batteries, engine manual). 'For a while it almost feels normal.'
'They don't sleep... they don't stop... like a river.' Leo runs from the water tower; fog on the horizon becomes THOUSANDS - a herd on Route 9 heading for the farm. MAYBE 6 HOURS.

Ruth has done the math (fence holds a few hundred, not thousands). Plan: don't fight, redirect - car stereo on the generator 1 mile east, lights out, wait in the dark. The groan, fingers rattling chain link... music starts, the herd turns east 'like a tide going out', all night. Sunrise: fence bent in three places but it held. Ruth: 'We're going to need a bigger fence.' Everyone laughs.

'So what would actually happen?' Infographic recap: cities fall first, supermarkets empty in days, grid fails in weeks, biggest danger = the living; survivors are not the strongest but the quiet ones who grow/fix/heal; don't try to survive alone.
Day 100 on the barn roof with Leo, potatoes ready, everyone in their place - then an engine sound: a plane contrail. 'Somebody out there is still flying.' Open-loop sequel tease.
'What's the first thing you'd grab if this happened tomorrow?' (italic on-screen text over the ensemble on the farm fence) + subscribe because 'this story isn't over yet'.

pacing.re_hook_interval_s: ~30-45 s: every chapter ends on a turn line ('Then the honking stops because the noise brought them', 'Simple plans never stay simple', 'which is exactly when you hear the engine', 'They're not infected, they're worse'); chapter cards / on-screen titles roughly every 60-90 s (12 YouTube chapters).
pacing.structure_ratio: Story ~80% / explainer facts ~20%, alternating: story set piece (40-90 s) -> 15-40 s factual interlude that justifies the next story turn -> back to story.
pacing.notes: Even, unhurried 155 wpm documentary pace; tension comes from short declarative sentences and pauses rather than speed. Visuals change every ~3-4 s with on-screen keyword captions reinforcing nearly every factual claim.

techniques_worth_copying: Second-person present tense ('You grab a backpack...') so the What-If is lived, not described - viewer is the protagonist.

Hybrid story + explainer: every factual interlude (R number, 3 days of food on shelves, grid failure, cities are death traps) directly sets up the next plot turn, so facts feel like stakes, not lectures.
Precise mundane anchors: '7:42 in the morning', 'kitchen knife you've never used for anything except tomatoes', 'shotgun for raccoons' - specificity + light humour humanise the dread.
Ensemble introduced with one-line name+role lower-thirds; each character gets one competence (nurse/clinic, driver/generator, kid/rifle) that pays off later.
Two sacrifice beats (Daniel walks out, Mr. Hale draws the horde) give emotional peaks at 5:10 and 7:15.
Thesis lines as full-frame text cards: 'THE SHUTTER CAN STOP THE DEAD. / IT CAN'T STOP THE LIVING.', 'SIMPLE PLANS NEVER STAY SIMPLE.'
Keyword captions in small letter-spaced caps on almost every factual shot (not word-by-word subtitles) - cheap to produce, reinforces retention.
Big circular face close-ups for reactions (wide eyes, wobbly mouth) cut between wide tiny-figure shots for scale contrast.
Counters and progress bars for numbers (infected 1 -> 64,565; items 29,835+; 3.0 -> 0.0 DAYS) - motion on data.
Sound visualised: concentric rings when the dock door screams, gun fires, radio broadcasts; noise is a plot mechanic.
Final 'So what would actually happen?' recap that turns the story into 5 takeaways, then an epilogue twist (plane contrail) as an open loop + comment-bait question ('first thing you'd grab').
Thumbnail: Day 1 vs Day N split-screen transformation with warm/cold colour split.

code_only_remake_needs.feasibility: High - the body of the video (0:09-14:10) is flat vector shapes, gradients, glows and line-art infographics, almost all achievable in Remotion + SVG. Only the 9 s cold open and the thumbnail use a richer painted/3D look that would need to be simplified.
code_only_remake_needs.character_rig: One reusable SVG stickman component: circle head (black fill + 2px rim-light stroke in a light colour), eye/eyebrow/mouth expression presets (neutral, worried wobbly mouth, wide-eyed, smug half-lid, crying with tear drops, angry), thin limb strokes with simple 2-3 pose keyframes (stand, walk cycle, run, sit, arms up, holding prop), shirt-colour prop and accessory slots (cap, ponytail, spiky hair, glasses, wide hat). Zombie variant = grey-green fill, glowing white eyes, red wound dots, arms-forward shamble cycle.
code_only_remake_needs.environment_kit: Parametric SVG backdrops: night skyline (random rect towers + lit windows), suburban house row, bedroom with window, supermarket aisles (procedural rows of coloured rectangles), storefront with sign + shutter, loading dock with lamp cone + box truck, highway of cars (top-down + side), gas station canopy, rolling-hill countryside with tree silhouettes, farm (red barn, water tower, chain-link pattern, house with lit windows). Three palettes: night navy, foggy pale blue, sunrise lavender-peach.
code_only_remake_needs.fx: Radial vignette, light cones (gradient polygons), bloom/glow filters, white flash frame, muzzle flash, concentric sound rings, fog bands, particle crowds (hundreds of dots/mini-zombies flowing like a river; Canvas for the 'thousands' shots), grid that fills red cell by cell, lights switching off on a dot grid, camera push-ins/pans via a transform wrapper, soft cross-dissolves.
code_only_remake_needs.infographics: Line-art components: neon stick-figure pictograms with highlight colour, branching infection tree, bar chart with growing bars + labels, animated counters, progress/depletion bar, icon flowchart (load -> dock -> drive), clock with shaded sector, top-down map with dashed route, inventory icon pop-ins.
code_only_remake_needs.typography: Letter-spaced uppercase geometric sans (Montserrat-like) for captions at ~2-3% frame height, white with red emphasis line; chapter cards ('DAY 1', 'DAY 5', '20 MINUTES LATER'); italic serif for the final CTA question; lower-third name/role cards.
code_only_remake_needs.audio: Local TTS narrator (calm male, ~155 wpm), ambient drone/piano bed, SFX library (buzz, scream, shutter slam, engine, BOOM, radio static, groan).
code_only_remake_needs.storyboard_density: ~240 shots over 14 min (avg 3.5 s) - needs a storyboard schema where each VO sentence maps to 1-2 shots with a backdrop id, actors + poses, caption text and a camera move, so the volume is template-driven rather than hand-animated.
